  2. Adverb Constantly during a certain period, or regularly at stated intervals (opposed to sometimes or occasionally).
  3. Adverb (informal) In any event.

am

  1. Verb first-person singular present indicative of be
  2. Contraction (informal or dialectal) Optional of I am.
  3. Adverb Alternative spelling of a.m.

amplified

  1. Verb simple past tense and past participle of amplify
  2. Adjective Having been made the subject of amplification; more potent or stronger, louder

an

  1. Article Form of a (all article senses).
  2. Article Used before a vowel sound.
  3. Article Used before /h/ in an unstressed syllable.
  4. Article (now quite rare) Used before one and words with initial u, eu.
  5. Article (nonstandard) Used before /h/ in a stressed syllable.
  6. Article (nonstandard, British, West Country) Used before all consonants.
  7. Numeral (nonstandard, British, West Country) one
  8. Conjunction (archaic) If
  9. Conjunction (archaic) So long as.
  10. Conjunction (archaic) As if; as though.
  11. Noun The first letter of the Georgian alphabet, ა (Mkhedruli), Ⴀ (Asomtavruli) or ⴀ (Nuskhuri).
  12. Preposition In each; to or for each; per.

and

  1. Conjunction As a coordinating conjunction; expressing two elements to be taken together or in addition to each other.
  2. Conjunction Used simply to connect two noun phrases, adjectives or adverbs.
  3. Conjunction Simply connecting two clauses or sentences.
  4. Conjunction Introducing a clause or sentence which follows on in time or consequence from the first.
  5. Conjunction (obsolete) Yet; but.
  6. Conjunction Used to connect certain numbers: connecting units when they precede tens (not dated); connecting tens and units to hundreds, thousands etc. (now often omitted in US); to connect fractions to wholes.
  7. Conjunction (now colloquial or literary) Used to connect more than two elements together in a chain, sometimes to stress the number of elements.
  8. Conjunction Connecting two identical elements, with implications of continued or infinite repetition.
  9. Conjunction Introducing a parenthetical or explanatory clause.
  10. Conjunction Introducing the continuation of narration from a previous understood point; also used alone as a question: ‘and so what?’.
  11. Conjunction (now regional or somewhat colloquial) Used to connect two verbs where the second is dependent on the first: ‘to’. Used especially after come, go and try.
  12. Conjunction Introducing a qualitative difference between things having the same name; "as well as other".
  13. Conjunction Used to combine numbers in addition; plus (with singular or plural verb).
  14. Conjunction (heading) Expressing a condition.
  15. Conjunction (now US dialect) If; provided that.
  16. Conjunction (obsolete) As if, as though.
  17. Conjunction (mathematics, logic) connecting two well-formed formulas to create a well formed formula that requires the new formula to only be true when each of the two are true.
  18. Noun (music, often informal) In rhythm, the second half of a divided beat.
  19. Noun (UK dialectal) Breath.
  20. Noun (UK dialectal) Sea smoke; steam fog.
  21. Verb (UK dialectal, intransitive) To breathe; whisper; devise; imagine.

angry

  1. Adjective Displaying or feeling anger.
  2. Adjective (said about a wound or a rash) Inflamed and painful.
  3. Adjective (figuratively, said about the elements, like the sky or the sea) Dark and stormy, menacing.
  4. Verb (obsolete) To anger.

animal

  1. Noun (science) A eukaryote of the clade Animalia; a multicellular organism that is usually mobile, whose cells are not encased in a rigid cell wall (distinguishing it from plants and fungi) and which derives energy solely from the consumption of other organisms (distinguishing it from plants).
  2. Noun (loosely) Any member of the kingdom Animalia other than a human.
  3. Noun (loosely, colloquial) Any land-living vertebrate (i.e. not fishes, insects, etc.).
  4. Noun (figuratively) A person who behaves wildly; a bestial, brutal, brutish, cruel, or inhuman person.
  5. Noun (informal) A person of a particular type.
  6. Noun Matter, thing.
  7. Adjective Of or relating to animals.
  8. Adjective Raw, base, unhindered by social codes.
  9. Adjective Pertaining to the spirit or soul; relating to sensation or innervation.
  10. Adjective (slang, Ireland) Excellent

anime

  1. Noun (uncountable) An artistic style originating in, and associated with, Japanese animation, and that has also been adopted by a comparatively low number of animated works from other countries.
  2. Noun (countable) An animated work that originated in Japan, regardless of the artistic style.
  3. Noun (rare, countable, chiefly proscribed) An animated work, regardless of the country of origin.
  4. Noun Alternative spelling of animé, the resin of the courbaril.

annoyed

  1. Adjective Causing irritation or annoyance; troublesome; vexatious.

  3. Noun (rare) That which annoys; an annoyance.

another

  6. Pronoun One of a group of things of the same kind.

  2. Noun Any fruit or vegetable, or any other thing produced by a plant such as a gall or cone, especially if produced by a tree and similar to the fruit of Malus domestica; also (with qualifying words) used to form the names of specific fruits such as custard apple, rose apple, thorn apple etc.

  6. Noun The Adam's apple.
  7. Noun (Christianity) The fruit of the Tree of Knowledge, eaten by Adam and Eve according to post-Biblical Christian tradition; the forbidden fruit.
  8. Noun A tree of the genus Malus, especially one cultivated for its edible fruit; the apple tree.

Adjective (Celtic linguistics, of a verb form) Used with no subject, indicating an unknown or unspecified agent; used in similar situations as the passive in English (the difference being that the theme in the English passive construction is the subject, while in the Celtic autonomous construction the theme is the object and there is no subject).

Noun (countable, logic, mathematics) A sequence of statements consisting of axioms, assumptions, statements already demonstrated in another proof, and statements that logically follow from previous statements in the sequence, and which concludes with a statement that is the object of the proof.

that

  1. Conjunction Introducing a clause which is the subject or object of a verb (such as one involving reported speech), or which is a complement to a previous statement.
  2. Conjunction Introducing a subordinate clause expressing a reason or cause: because, in that.
  3. Conjunction (dated) Introducing a subordinate clause that expresses an aim, purpose, or goal ("final"), and usually contains the auxiliaries may, might, or should: so, so that.
  4. Conjunction Introducing — especially, but not exclusively, with an antecedent like so or such — a subordinate clause expressing a result, consequence, or effect.
  5. Conjunction (archaic or poetic) Introducing a premise or supposition for consideration: seeing as; inasmuch as; given that; as would appear from the fact that.
  6. Conjunction Introducing a subordinate clause modifying an adverb.
  7. Conjunction (archaic or poetic) Introducing an exclamation expressing a desire or wish.
  8. Conjunction Introducing an exclamation expressing a strong emotion such as sadness or surprise.
  9. Determiner The (thing, person, idea, etc) indicated or understood from context, especially if more remote physically, temporally or mentally than one designated as "this", or if expressing distinction.
  10. Pronoun (demonstrative) The thing, person, idea, quality, event, action, or time indicated or understood from context, especially if more remote geographically, temporally or mentally than one designated as "this", or if expressing distinction.
  11. Pronoun The known (thing); used to refer to something just said.
  12. Pronoun (demonstrative) The aforementioned quality or proposition; used to emphatically affirm or deny a previous statement or question.
  13. Pronoun (relative) (plural that) Which, who; representing a subject, direct object, indirect object, or object of a preposition.
  14. Pronoun (colloquial) Used in place of relative adverbs such as where or when; often omitted.
  15. Pronoun (Northern England, Manchester, Liverpool) Clipping of that is; used to reinforce the preceding assertion or statement.
  16. Adverb (degree) To a given extent or degree.
  17. Adverb (degree) To a great extent or degree; very, particularly (in negative constructions).
  18. Adverb (informal, Britain, Australia) To such an extent; so. (in positive constructions).

the

  1. Article Definite grammatical article that implies necessarily that an entity it hints at is presupposed; something already mentioned, or completely specified later in that same sentence, or assumed already completely specified.
  2. Article Used before a noun modified by a restrictive relative clause, indicating that the noun refers to a single referent defined by the relative clause.
  3. Article Used before an object considered to be unique, or of which there is only one at a time.
  4. Article Used before a superlative or an ordinal number modifying a noun, to indicate that the noun refers to a single item.
  5. Article Added to a superlative or an ordinal number to make it into a substantive.
  6. Article Introducing a singular term to be taken generically: preceding a name of something standing for a whole class.
  7. Article Used before an adjective, indicating all things (especially persons) described by that adjective.
  8. Article Used to indicate a certain example of (a noun) which is usually of most concern or most common or familiar.
  9. Article Used before a body part (especially of someone previously mentioned), as an alternative to a possessive pronoun.
  10. Article When stressed, indicates that it describes an object which is considered to be best or exclusively worthy of attention.
  11. Adverb With a comparative or with more and a verb phrase, establishes a correlation with one or more other such comparatives.
  12. Adverb With a comparative, and often with for it, indicates a result more like said comparative. This can be negated with none.
  13. Preposition For each; per.

Noun (countable, law, real estate, obsolete) An obsolete legal agreement that was a real covenant and ran with the land, whereby the grantor and his heirs of a piece of real estate held in freehold were required to officially guarantee their claim and plead one’s case for the title. If evicted by someone with a superior claim (paramount title) they were also required to hand over other real estate of equal value in recompense. It has now been replaced by personal covenants and the covenant of warranty.

Noun (countable, law) A legal agreement, either written or oral (an expressed warranty) or implied through the actions of the buyer and seller (an implied warranty), which states that the goods or property in question will be in exactly the same state as promised, such as in a sale of an item or piece of real estate.

  7. Pronoun (fused relative) That which; those that; the thing(s) that.
  8. Pronoun (fused relative) Anything that; all that; whatever.
  9. Pronoun (relative, nonstandard) That; which; who.
  10. Adverb (interrogative) In what way; to what extent.
  11. Adverb Used before a prepositional phrase to emphasise that something is taken into consideration as a cause or reason; usually used in combination with 'with' (see what with), and much less commonly with other prepositions.
  12. Interjection An expression of surprise or disbelief.
  13. Interjection What do you want? An abrupt, usually unfriendly enquiry as to what a person desires.
  14. Interjection (British, colloquial, dated) Clipping of what do you say? Used as a type of tag question to emphasise a statement and invite agreement, often rhetorically.
  15. Interjection What did you say? I beg your pardon?

  17. Noun (obsolete, uncountable) Something; thing; stuff.
  18. Noun (countable) The identity of a thing, as an answer to a question of what.
  19. Noun (countable) Something that is addressed by what, as opposed to a person, addressed by who.
  20. Particle (Manglish, Singlish) Emphasizes the truth of an assertion made to contradict an evidently false assumption held by the listener.

whatever
